implementation_notes: Default JVM realization and the pattern's canonical API: the provider keeps the subscription record and the backlog, and the client only re-attaches by name. Choose it when the broker is a JMS provider (ActiveMQ Artemis, IBM MQ, Solace, Service Bus over AMQP) and the subscription lifecycle should be managed through the API.
pitfalls: The backlog grows until unacknowledged messages expire or unsubscribe(name) is called; orphan subscriptions are a common broker-storage leak.
Shared and unshared durable subscriptions cannot share name and client id; mixing them throws.

variants.name: Kafka consumer group with manual commitSync
variants.implementation_notes: Where Kafka is the broker, the consumer group and its committed offsets are the durable position, stored in __consumer_offsets and bounded by offset retention (default seven days). Choose it when the same log must serve many heterogeneous consumers and replay is a normal operational tool.
pitfalls: Auto-commit (the default) records progress before processing; disable it or accept loss on crash.
Offsets expire when the group stays empty past offsets.retention.minutes; after that the group resumes per auto.offset.reset.
